bib.title: PAWS: Paraphrase Adversaries from Word Scrambling

question: Can a paraphrase dataset built from high-lexical-overlap pairs expose, and help fix, models' insensitivity to word order and structure?
hypothesis: Performance on high-overlap pairs depends on the number of representative training examples and on a model's ability to represent non-local context and cross-sentence word interaction.
contributions: A workflow (LM-controlled word swapping plus back translation plus human judgment) for generating balanced high-overlap paraphrase/non-paraphrase pairs
PAWS dataset: 108,463 pairs from Quora and Wikipedia
Evaluation of six models showing state-of-the-art models fail without PAWS training and BERT/DIIN recover with it

method.summary: Pairs are generated by constrained beam search word swapping under a one-billion-word LM and by English-German-English back translation, then rated by five annotators. Six paraphrase models are trained on QQP, QQP+PAWS, or PAWS-Wiki and evaluated on QQP and PAWS.

datasets.name: QQP
datasets.split: standard train/dev/test; 16,280 raw swapped QQP pairs sent to humans

datasets.name: PAWS-QQP
datasets.split: train 11,988; dev 677; no test; train is subset of QQP train, dev subset of QQP dev and test
datasets.source: swapped QQP sentences, 5 human ratings each, keep 4-of-5 agreement; trivial identical pairs removed from dev/test
datasets.preprocessing: Sentence correction then paraphrase judgment; source/generated sentences randomly flipped

datasets.name: PAWS-Wiki
datasets.split: train 49,401; dev 8,000; test 8,000; no source-sentence overlap across sets
datasets.source: Wikipedia dumps; swapping (50k raw) plus back translation (26,897 pairs)

datasets.name: PAWS-Wiki-Swap
datasets.source: human-labelled swapped Wikipedia pairs with no back-translation counterpart

datasets.name: Unlabeled PAWS-Wiki
datasets.source: swap pairs labelled non-paraphrase, back-translation pairs labelled paraphrase

models.name: BERT-base
models.params: inferred: over 100m (text says BERT has over 100m)
models.architecture: Transformer encoder, one extra output layer
models.init_from: released BERT-base pretrained model (pretrained on over three billion words)

models.name: BiLSTM and BOW cosine baselines
models.architecture: BOW: unigram+bigram encodings; BiLSTM encoder; cosine above .5 = paraphrase

other.bert: authors' default fine-tuning configuration, BERT-base chosen over BERT-large due to GPU memory limits
other.others: own re-implementations matching reported QQP performance; 300-d GloVe embeddings, fixed during training
other.generation: word swapping: CRF POS tagger, NER entity tags if prob >95%, LM from 1B-word benchmark, beam size 100, threshold t=3.0; back translation: top k=5 each way, English-German NMT trained on WMT14 (Wu et al. 2016 architecture), BOW cosine >=0.9, at least half of pairs inversion rate >0.02

inference.samples: single run per setting; no seeds reported

eval.protocol: Test sets for QQP and PAWS-Wiki; dev set for PAWS-QQP (no test). No variance or significance tests.

availability.code: BERT: github.com/google-research/bert; own model code not stated

results.claim: BERT trained on QQP only scores 33.5% accuracy on PAWS-QQP, versus 90.5% on QQP.
results.setup: Quora Question Pairs, BERT-base fine-tuned with default config; evaluated on PAWS-QQP dev set (677 pairs), trained on QQP train only

results.claim: Adding PAWS-QQP training pairs lifts BERT to 85.0% accuracy on PAWS-QQP (+51.5).
results.setup: Quora Question Pairs, BERT-base fine-tuned with default config; evaluated on PAWS-QQP dev set (677 pairs), trained on QQP+PAWS-QQP train (11,988 PAWS pairs)

results.claim: BERT AUC on PAWS-QQP rises from 35.1 to 83.1 with PAWS training.
results.setup: Quora Question Pairs, BERT-base fine-tuned with default config; evaluated on PAWS-QQP dev set (677 pairs)

results.claim: Adding PAWS-QQP does not hurt QQP accuracy for BERT.
results.quote: a BERT model ﬁne-tuned on QQP+PAWSQQP achieves the same 90.5% classification accuracy as training on QQP alone

results.claim: BERT-base supervised on PAWS-Wiki human-labelled data reaches 90.4% accuracy on the test set; with silver-label pretraining 91.9%.
results.setup: PAWS-Wiki test (8,000 pairs), BERT-base, supervised only
results.table: Table 8, row BERT, column Supervised (Acc); Pretrain+Fine-tune Acc 91.9

results.claim: DIIN (590k params) is nearly as good as BERT on PAWS-QQP: 83.8% accuracy with PAWS vs 32.8% without.
results.table: Table 7, row DIIN (Gong et al., 2018), column QQP+PAWSQQP→PAWSQQP (Acc)

results.claim: The BOW model learns almost nothing from PAWS-QQP training (29.0 to 30.0% accuracy).
results.setup: BOW encoder, QQP+PAWS-QQP training, PAWS-QQP dev

results.claim: All models score under 40% accuracy on PAWS-QQP when trained on QQP alone, despite over 83% on QQP.
results.setup: six models trained on QQP train, tested on PAWS-QQP dev
results.quote: all models, including BERT, obtain abysmal accuracy under 40%

results.claim: Gap between BiLSTM and BERT is 4.2% on QQP but 27% on PAWS-QQP, a 60% relative error reduction.
results.note: Table 7 gives 86.3 vs 90.5 on QQP and 57.6 vs 85.0 on PAWS-QQP.
results.quote: the absolute difference between BiLSTM and BERT is 4.2% on QQP, but it goes up to 27% on PAWSQQP, which is a 60% relative reduction in error

results.claim: With 6,000 PAWS-QQP training examples both DIIN and BERT go from 30% to 74% AUC; curves have not converged.
results.setup: DIIN and BERT, QQP plus varying PAWS-QQP counts, read from Fig 4 per text
results.quote: Both models improve from 30% to 74% AUC scores with 6,000 PAWSQQP examples

results.claim: Silver-label pretraining on unlabelled PAWS-Wiki (656k pairs) helps all models except BOW and vanilla DecAtt.
results.setup: Pretrain on silver labels then fine-tune on human labels, PAWS-Wiki test
results.quote: The result is a total of 656k pairs with silver labels.

results.claim: DIIN trained on QQP+PAWS-QQP gets 70.5% AUC on PAWS-Wiki, vs 46.0% with no PAWS data and 92.9% with in-domain PAWS-Wiki.
results.quote: Table 9 shows that a DIIN model trained on Quora (QQP+PAWSQQP) achieves 70.5% AUC on the Wikipedia domain.

results.claim: Training on both domains gives 9.2 point AUC gain on PAWS-QQP over QQP+PAWS-QQP.
results.setup: DIIN, QQP+PAWS-QQP+Wiki vs QQP+PAWS-QQP, PAWS-QQP dev
results.quote: leads to 9.2% absolute AUC gains on PAWSQQP

results.claim: Of 687 BERT mistakes on PAWS-Wiki test, DIIN got 280 (41%) right, so errors are weakly correlated.
results.unit: % of BERT errors DIIN gets right
results.quote: of 687 of BERT’s mistakes on the PAWSWiki test set, DIIN got 280 (41%) correct

results.claim: PAWS has 108,463 human-labelled pairs in total.
results.quote: There are 108,463 PAWS pairs in total.

results.claim: In QQP only about 20% of the roughly 1,000 pairs with identical BOW are non-paraphrases.
results.quote: of the ∼1,000 pairs with the same BOW, only 20% are not paraphrases

results.claim: Human agreement with majority vote is 92.0% (Quora) and 94.7% (Wikipedia) on swapped pairs, rising to 95.8% and 97.5% after keeping only 4-of-5 or 5-of-5 agreement.
results.setup: five annotators per pair, binary label
results.quote: human agreement is high on both Quora (92.0%) and Wikipedia (94.7%)

results.claim: Swapping yields mostly non-paraphrases (67% QQP, 88% Wikipedia); back translation yields 94.9% paraphrases.
results.quote: most of the examples (94.9%) are paraphrases (as expected)

limits: No variance, seeds or significance tests; no hyperparameters beyond BERT defaults.
PAWS-QQP has no test set, so results are on a 677-pair dev set.
Only BERT-base was tried; BERT-large not run for GPU memory.
Authors concede learning curves have not converged, so more PAWS data would likely help.
Only English; generation is limited to pairs the LM and constraints accept (about 3% of candidates).
Models were not newly developed; the paper does not propose a method that solves PAWS.
